title: The Unofficial Prom
premise: Edmund Oyelaran, a scholarship senior at Hollowmere Academy, has spent four years perfecting invisibility—until the college essay prompt 'What tradition would you die to protect?' cracks him open. His answer accidentally exposes the Unofficial Prom, a century-old secret dance where the town's founding families have quietly decided who belongs and who doesn't, and whose corruption Edmund's late mother once documented in a hidden ledger. When the founding families move to bury the tradition—and the evidence with it—Edmund must rally the misfits he's kept at arm's length to stage one last honest Prom before the final football game, forcing the town to choose between its myth and its truth.
about_author: Freya Ashgrove is a former boarding school scholarship kid who writes about the students history forgets to name. She lives in a small town that still argues about its own founding story.

chapters.title: The Question on Page Forty-Seven
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. During a college essay workshop, the prompt 'What tradition would you die to protect?' makes the whole class go quiet—including golden boy Whit Ashcombe. Edmund writes something honest for the first time in years and immediately regrets it. Emotional beat: the terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Invisible by Design
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Flashback-woven chapter establishing his scholarship-kid survival rules at Hollowmere: never first, never last, never noticed. His job at the town diner puts him adjacent to every secret without owning any. Beat: comfort and cost of hiding.

chapters.title: The Essay That Walked Away
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. His draft essay vanishes from the shared drive and resurfaces in Whit's hands. Instead of mockery, Whit asks one question: 'You know about the Prom, don't you?' Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Town Won't Say
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Priya Chandrasekaran, editor of the school paper, has been chasing rumors of the Unofficial Prom for two years. She corners Edmund after finding his name in an old guest list. Beat: reluctant alliance formed over shared hunger for truth.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Cruelties
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Searching his mother's stored boxes for college paperwork, he finds her hidden ledger documenting decades of Prom decisions—who was invited, who was ruined, who left town. Her handwriting stops abruptly eleven years ago. Beat: grief recontextualized as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Founding Families' Dinner
chapters.summary: Whit's POV. Whit endures the annual Ashcombe dinner where his father and the other founding heirs discuss 'managing the essay situation.' Whit realizes he's a pawn being groomed to inherit the machinery. Beat: complicity curdling into nausea.

chapters.title: Rules of the Dance
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya and Edmund decode the ledger: the Prom isn't a party, it's a tribunal—a beautiful ritual where invitations confer belonging and exclusions destroy families. The last game of the season is when this year's Prom would happen. Beat: the scale of the secret lands.

chapters.title: Misfits, Assembled
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund, against every instinct, recruits the excluded: diner coworker Marcus, theater kid June, quiet transfer student Bea. Each has a family wound the Prom caused. Beat: found family forming out of shared damage.

chapters.title: Whit Defects
chapters.summary: Whit's POV. Whit brings his father's stolen planning documents to the group, confessing his childhood role as the heir who delivered the 'no' letters. Edmund must decide whether betrayal can be inherited or only chosen. Beat: forgiveness tested.

chapters.title: The First Crack
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The paper publishes a carefully vague feature about 'lost traditions,' and the town erupts. Edmund's scholarship status is suddenly 'under review.' Beat: power shows its teeth; fear spreads through the group.

chapters.title: June's Mother's Year
chapters.summary: June's POV. June reveals her mother was Prom-queen'd then destroyed in 2004—the ledger's cruelest entry. The group realizes the tradition doesn't just exclude outsiders; it consumes insiders who step out of line. Beat: stakes become personal and generational.

chapters.title: An Offer He Should Refuse
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Headmaster Voss offers Edmund full ride to any college, plus his mother's sealed personnel file—if he returns the ledger and disavows the story. The file might explain why she stopped writing. Beat: temptation weaponized against grief.

chapters.title: What Mom Knew
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Whit helps Edmund access the sealed file: his mother wasn't fired, she resigned mid-investigation because the families threatened her son's future enrollment. She chose him over the truth. Beat: anger at her dissolving into devastating understanding.

chapters.title: The Plan Nobody Agrees On
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The group debates: expose the Prom publicly, or reclaim it—stage their own honest Prom before the final game, inviting everyone, forcing the town to watch what its tradition really looks like when stripped of cruelty. Beat: strategy forged through conflict.

chapters.title: Sabotage Season
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Retaliation escalates: Marcus loses his job, June's theater program is defunded, Bea's visa 'complication' appears. The founding families are dismantling the group piece by piece. Beat: despair, and the choice to hold anyway.

chapters.title: Bea's Gamble
chapters.summary: Bea's POV. Bea leaks scanned ledger pages anonymously, timing them to homecoming week. The town splits down old fault lines; some elders privately thank her, admitting they were 'uninvited' too. Beat: hope arriving sideways.

chapters.title: Voss's Confession
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Headmaster Voss, himself uninvited decades ago, quietly unlocks the old gymnasium—the original Prom site—for them, saying 'Some debts you pay forward.' Beat: unexpected allyship; the venue secured.

chapters.title: Everything Falls Apart
chapters.summary: Whit's POV. Whit's father discovers the plan, disowns him publicly, and gets the gym condemned via emergency inspection. The game is tomorrow; the Prom has no venue, and half the group wants to quit. Beat: all-is-lost nadir.

chapters.title: The Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. At halftime of the final game, the group hijacks the PA and field: lights up, music on, and every student, teacher, and townsfolk uninvited across a century walks onto the field. The Unofficial Prom happens in plain sight. Beat: triumphant climax.

chapters.title: Ashcombe's Last Invitation
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Whit's father confronts Edmund at midfield, offering everything back if the dance stops. Edmund refuses—not with rage but with the ledger read aloud over the speakers. The crowd stays dancing. Beat: power broken by witness, not war.

chapters.title: After the Music
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Fallout: investigations open, Voss resigns contentedly, Whit rebuilds his relationship with his father slowly, and the essay question gets answered honestly in a hundred college applications. Beat: consequences with tenderness.

chapters.title: What I Would Die to Protect
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, epilogue. Edmund submits his final essay—not about the Prom, but about the misfits who became his family and the mother who chose him. He gets into college, but the real ending is the group's promise: next year, everyone's invited. Beat: inheritance rewritten as belonging.
